claim: After RSI(2) below 10, RSI(14) below 30 or a close below the lower Bollinger band, SPY and QQQ bought at the next open beat random entries.
result: 6 of 12 next-open pricings rated Lead. Since 2010, buy-and-hold at the same exposure earned more per unit of drawdown in every Lead. Forward: page stance log since the 2026-11-06 close (4 records).
test: Trade simulation with random-entry test, exposure-matched buy-and-hold and the 1993-2009 holdout; then the page's stance log.
title: Oversold bounce, bought at the next open

claim: Part of the oversold bounce happens overnight, so the closing-price entry is better than the next open.
result: Close entry had the higher mean per trade in all 5 rules where both are Leads (SPY Bollinger +0.54% vs +0.46%, QQQ RSI(2) +0.60% vs +0.48%). SPY RSI(2) hold 5 is a Lead only at the close. Not usable yet: the page is built after the close.
test: Same trades priced at the signal close and at the next open.
title: Buying at the signal close beats the next open

claim: After a normal down day, SPY held five sessions beats random entries.
result: Survives the 1993-2009 holdout but is mostly beta: +0.34% per trade gross vs +0.25% for random entries in the same windows. First forward signal: 2026-11-12 close.
test: Frozen paper experiment (four rules), logged before each open.
title: Normal drop: long for five sessions

claim: After a big up day, shorting SPY for one or five sessions is profitable.
result: All three failed the holdout. They stay in the frozen paper experiment, which cannot be changed, but are not used.
test: Development period, then the untouched 1993-2009 holdout.
title: Rally shorts (three rules)

claim: EMA touches, MACD crosses, breakouts, volume spikes or the 200-day state predict the next days.
result: No evidence. Only the oversold mean-reversion rules were candidates.
test: 90 daily indicator tests with a multiple-testing correction and the 1993-2009 holdout.
title: Trend and momentum indicators

claim: A break of the first 15 minutes' range confirmed by VWAP continues through the session.
result: 5 prototype trades only, from before the liquidity gate. Blocked until the gate has 20 complete sampled days.
test: Registered intraday rule on minute bars, behind the 20-session liquidity gate.
title: Opening-range break with VWAP (orb-continuation-v1)

claim: Next-open oversold trades do worse when the open gaps up strongly from the signal close.
test: Split the next-open trades by gap size in the backtester, with the buckets fixed before running.
title: A large overnight gap uses up the bounce

claim: The oversold rules behave differently by trend (above or below the 200-day average) and VIX level.
test: One pre-registered trend-and-volatility filter as a new backtester version, checked once on the holdout.
title: Oversold rules depend on the regime

claim: A rule that looks fired at 3:50 PM ET is nearly always still fired at 4:00 PM.
test: Flip rate between the 3:50 PM price and the close, from the collected minute bars, once enough sessions exist.
title: A signal seen at 3:50 PM holds to the close

claim: On some kinds of day the at-the-money 0DTE straddle prices more or less movement than SPY and QQQ deliver.
test: Collect the 9:45 AM same-day straddle and compare with the move to the close, by regime and event day; first read after 60 sessions.
title: Same-day options: implied move against realised move

claim: The oversold trades keep their edge when held in TQQQ or UPRO instead of QQQ or SPY.
test: Price the same historical trades in the leveraged ETFs (2010 on, so no 1993-2009 holdout).
title: Evidence priced in the leveraged ETFs
